name: Media codec and capability probing
plain: Asks which audio and video codecs, containers and DRM systems the browser supports.
meaning: Hardware decoders for HEVC, AV1 and DRM (Widevine, FairPlay, PlayReady) differ by OS and chip, so the map reveals device class and licensing.

steps: Test 50 to 200 MIME and codec strings
Query MediaCapabilities for smooth and powerEfficient flags

safari.note: macOS first, iPhone MSE from 17.1 via ManagedMediaSource

data.metric: Bit vector plus power efficiency flags

limits.headline: Can ask which video, audio and copy protection formats your device supports
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Ask if your device plays formats such as HEVC and AV1
Check for copy protection systems such as Widevine, FairPlay and PlayReady
Guess your system, chip and device type from the answers
cannot: See what you watch on other sites
Know who you are by itself

story.what_it_is: A page asks which audio and video formats and copy protection systems your browser can play.

marketing.name: Media Capabilities API
marketing.pitch: Lets a site ask whether the device can decode a video smoothly and efficiently before it picks a stream.

story.for_you: You never see it. When you press play, the site first asks your browser which formats it can handle, then picks the best one. You get smoother video and fewer stalls.
story.for_makers: Streaming and cloud gaming services need it to send the right stream, such as H.264, HEVC or AV1, without wasting data or battery. The same answers also work as a device clue for fraud and tracking tools.

use_cases.example: Netflix checks which video formats and copy protection your browser supports, then streams you the best picture it can.
Xbox Cloud Gaming and GeForce NOW in a browser check which video formats your device can decode, so the game stream is sharp and has low delay.
A live sports or concert stream picks a format your phone decodes in hardware, to save battery.
A video call site checks codecs before it starts, to use the one your device runs best.
A fraud tool compares the format list to the device's claimed model, to catch emulators.
A tracker adds the format list to a device ID, since it differs by browser, chip and system.
A web class platform picks smaller video for older laptops so lessons still play.

technical_bounds: No codec data for media the person plays
Entropy is mostly browser and OS
